title: Ballyhoo, portable stage and carbon lights
summary: The show advertised by playing from the bus, then set up a portable stage lit by carbon lights.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: You said...I forget...it came up, something about when the people were there or something. Did the people turn out to see the medicine show, or did you start playing to bring the people in? Were they there before you started playing, or...?

Oh yeah. When we first got to town, we advertised. Just by playing. They didn't put out anything like a circus has their little posters and things. It wasn't nothin' like that. We just brought the people by ballyhooing, they called it -- playing on the back of that bus, on that little platform. Then we'd go into this lot where we was gonna play. And we had a portable platform, that that guy that would cook on the bus, he would help, and we would help, too, to set that platform up. But it was the stage, in other words. It was a half stage and there was a kind of curtain like, and we'd dress in the back there, and they had a little ladder that you climb up the stage that was, oh, I don't know, like maybe...at least four-and-a-half feet high. And they had these carbon lights. They never had no electric lights.

Carbon lights is a solution that you put in a little tank, and they had a little kind of a metal rig, and they put this solution in there (and I don't know exactly what the mixture was), and they had a little pump on it, and you'd pump air in it, and it would form a gas...

And some of them just had regular lamps. Some of them, the poor ones, they had a torch maybe or something that they would use. But Doc and Doc's show... Doc was first-class, so he had these nice lights.
